Combine and serve: Add the charred chicken pieces to the sauce, stir to coat, and simmer for a further 5 minutes until the chicken is heated through and has absorbed the flavours. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve: Spoon the butter chicken alongside the fluffy basmati rice and garnish generously with fresh coriander leaves.
_brief: Butter chicken with basmati rice

title: Chana Masala with Spinach
description: A deeply aromatic, restaurant-worthy chana masala with tender chickpeas and wilted spinach cooked in a richly spiced tomato-onion masala.

ingredients.name: canned chickpeas
ingredients.raw: 800g canned chickpeas (2 cans), drained and rinsed

ingredients.name: green chillies
ingredients.raw: 2 green chillies, finely chopped (seeds in for heat)

ingredients.name: fresh coriander
ingredients.raw: small handful fresh coriander, roughly chopped, to serve

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.raw: ½ lemon, juice only, to finish

steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan or kadai over medium-high heat. Once shimmering, add the mustard seeds and cumin seeds and fry for 30–40 seconds until they begin to splutter.
Add the diced onions and a pinch of salt. Fry, stirring frequently, for 12–15 minutes until deep golden brown — this caramelisation is key to an authentic masala base.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the minced garlic, grated ginger, and green chillies. Stir and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the ground coriander, ground cumin, turmeric, and Kashmiri chilli powder. Stir vigorously for 1 minute to toast the spices in the oil, adding a splash of water if they begin to stick.

Add the tomato purée and stir for 1 minute, then pour in the canned tomatoes. Cook on medium heat for 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the masala has thickened and the oil separates slightly at the edges.

Add the drained chickpeas and 150ml water. Stir well to coat in the masala. Partially cover and simmer on medium-low heat for 12–15 minutes until the chickpeas are tender and the sauce has deepened in colour.
Lightly mash about a quarter of the chickpeas against the side of the pan with the back of a spoon — this naturally thickens the gravy.
Stir in the amchur powder and garam masala. Taste and adjust salt.
Add the fresh spinach in two batches, folding it through the curry and allowing each batch to wilt fully before adding the next, about 2–3 minutes total.
Squeeze over the lemon juice, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve hot with basmati rice, naan, or bhatura.
_brief: Chana masala with spinach

title: Goan Fish Curry with Coconut
description: A vibrant, tangy Goan fish curry simmered in a rich coconut milk gravy with warming spices, fresh chillies, and a signature tamarind kick.

ingredients.name: firm white fish fillets (such as kingfish, cod, or snapper)
ingredients.raw: 600 g firm white fish fillets (such as kingfish, cod, or snapper), cut into large chunks

ingredients.name: dried Kashmiri red chillies
ingredients.raw: 4 dried Kashmiri red chillies (soaked in warm water for 10 mins)

steps: Dry-toast the coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and black peppercorns in a small frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes until fragrant. Transfer to a spice grinder or pestle and mortar and grind to a fine powder.

Drain the soaked Kashmiri chillies and blend them together with the garlic cloves, ginger, ground spice mix, and turmeric with 3–4 tablespoons of water to form a smooth, vibrant spice paste. Set aside.
Heat the coconut oil in a large, deep pan or wok over medium heat. Add the curry leaves and sliced onion and fry for 8–10 minutes, stirring regularly, until the onion is soft and golden.
Add the spice paste to the pan and cook, stirring constantly, for 3–4 minutes until the raw smell disappears and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Add the chopped tomatoes and slit green chillies. Cook for a further 4–5 minutes, mashing the tomatoes down until they break apart and are fully incorporated into the sauce.
Pour in the coconut milk and tamarind paste. Stir well to combine, then bring the curry to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 minutes to let the sauce thicken slightly and the flavours meld.

Season with salt, then gently lower the fish chunks into the simmering curry. Cook undisturbed for 7–8 minutes, or until the fish is just cooked through and flakes easily — do not stir vigorously to keep the pieces intact.
Taste and adjust salt or tamarind as needed. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot with steamed basmati rice.
_brief: Goan fish curry with coconut

title: Authentic Prawn Pad Thai
description: A sizzling, street-food-style Pad Thai packed with plump prawns, silky rice noodles, and a perfectly balanced tamarind-fish sauce glaze, topped with crunchy peanuts and fresh lime.

ingredients.name: dried sen lek rice noodles (3mm flat)
ingredients.raw: 200g dried sen lek rice noodles (3mm flat)

ingredients.name: raw king prawns, peeled and deveined
ingredients.raw: 250g raw king prawns, peeled and deveined

ingredients.name: palm sugar (or soft brown sugar)
ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp palm sugar (or soft brown sugar)

ingredients.name: extra-firm tofu, cut into small cubes
ingredients.raw: 80g extra-firm tofu, cut into small cubes

ingredients.name: roasted unsalted peanuts, roughly crushed
ingredients.raw: 4 tbsp roasted unsalted peanuts, roughly crushed

ingredients.name: dried chilli flakes
ingredients.raw: 1 tsp dried chilli flakes, plus extra to serve

steps: Soak the dried rice noodles in a large bowl of room-temperature water for 30 minutes until pliable but still firm (do not use boiling water). Drain and set aside.

Mix the Pad Thai sauce: whisk together the tamarind paste, fish sauce, oyster sauce, and palm sugar in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves. Taste — it should be a balanced mix of sour, salty, and slightly sweet. Adjust if needed.
Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a wok over high heat until smoking. Add the tofu cubes and fry for 3–4 minutes, turning, until golden on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Add another 1 tbsp of oil to the wok. Add the prawns in a single layer and sear for 1–2 minutes each side until pink and just cooked through. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp of oil to the wok over high heat. Fry the garlic and shallots for 1 minute until fragrant and lightly golden.

Add the dried shrimp and stir-fry for 30 seconds, then add the drained noodles. Pour the Pad Thai sauce over the noodles and toss everything together using tongs for 1–2 minutes until the noodles are well coated and beginning to caramelise slightly.
Push the noodles to one side of the wok. Crack in both eggs and scramble them briefly, then fold them into the noodles before they are fully set.
Return the cooked prawns and tofu to the wok. Add the bean sprouts and spring onions, and toss everything together over high heat for 1 minute so the sprouts retain a little crunch.
Divide between two plates. Top with crushed peanuts, dried chilli flakes, and fresh coriander. Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side for squeezing.
_brief: Pad thai with prawns

title: Thai Basil Beef (Pad Krapow Neua) with Jasmine Rice
description: A fiery, fragrant Thai street-food classic — tender minced beef stir-fried with garlic, birds-eye chillies, and a generous heap of fresh holy basil, served over fluffy jasmine rice.

ingredients.name: fresh holy basil leaves
ingredients.raw: 1 large handful fresh holy basil leaves (or Thai basil as substitute)

ingredients.name: birds-eye red chillies
ingredients.raw: 4 birds-eye red chillies, roughly chopped (adjust to heat preference)

steps: Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Combine with 420ml water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then reduce to the lowest heat, cover tightly, and cook for 12 minutes. Remove from heat and leave covered for 5 minutes to steam.
In a small bowl, mix together the oyster sauce, fish sauce, thin soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and sugar. Set aside.
Using a pestle and mortar (or the flat of a knife), roughly pound the garlic and birds-eye chillies together into a coarse paste — keep some texture.
Heat a wok over the highest possible heat until smoking. Add 1½ tbsp of vegetable oil, then fry the garlic-chilli paste for 30 seconds until deeply fragrant and just golden.
Add the sliced shallots and stir-fry for 1 minute until softened.
Add the beef mince, breaking it up immediately with a spatula. Stir-fry on high heat for 3–4 minutes until the beef is well browned with slightly crispy edges.
Pour the sauce mixture over the beef and toss everything together for 1 minute until the beef is evenly coated and glossy.
Remove the wok from heat and fold in the holy basil leaves, tossing until just wilted from the residual heat.
In a separate small frying pan, heat the remaining ½ tbsp oil over high heat. Crack in the eggs and fry for 1½–2 minutes until the whites are crispy and lacy at the edges but the yolk is still runny.
Spoon the jasmine rice into bowls, top generously with the Thai basil beef, and crown each bowl with a crispy fried egg. Serve immediately.
_brief: Thai basil beef with jasmine rice

title: Thai Green Curry with Chicken and Thai Basil
description: A fragrant, creamy Thai green curry brimming with tender chicken, silky coconut milk, and a fresh burst of Thai basil — authentically bold and beautifully aromatic.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.raw: 500 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, sliced into bite-sized pieces

ingredients.name: palm sugar
ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp palm sugar (or light brown sugar)

ingredients.name: lemongrass stalk
ingredients.raw: 1 lemongrass stalk, bruised and cut into 3 pieces

ingredients.name: Thai basil leaves
ingredients.raw: 1 large handful fresh Thai basil leaves

ingredients.name: Thai eggplant
ingredients.raw: 150 g Thai eggplant, quartered (or regular eggplant, cubed)

ingredients.name: long red chilli
ingredients.raw: 1 long red chilli, sliced, to garnish

steps: Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until clear, then cook according to packet instructions. Keep warm until serving.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large heavy-based saucepan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add the green curry paste and fry for 1–2 minutes, stirring constantly, until very fragrant and the oil begins to separate.
Pour in roughly half the coconut milk (about 200 ml) and stir vigorously to combine with the paste. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves, then stir and cook for 2 minutes to infuse the base.
Add the sliced chicken thighs and toss to coat in the curry base. Cook for 4–5 minutes, turning occasionally, until the chicken is sealed on all sides.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and the chicken stock. Stir in the fish sauce and palm sugar.
Add the Thai eggplant and bring the curry to a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered for 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the eggplant is tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the baby spinach and let it wilt for 1 minute. Taste and adjust seasoning — add more fish sauce for saltiness or palm sugar for sweetness.
Remove from the heat and stir in most of the Thai basil leaves, reserving a few for garnish.
Remove and discard the lemongrass, galangal slices, and kaffir lime leaves.
Ladle the curry into bowls over jasmine rice. Garnish with the reserved Thai basil and sliced red chilli. Serve immediately.
_brief: Green curry with chicken and Thai basil

title: Chicken Tinga Tacos with Lime Slaw
description: Smoky, chipotle-braised shredded chicken piled into warm corn tortillas and crowned with a bright, tangy lime slaw — authentic Mexican street-food magic on your plate.

ingredients.name: white onion
ingredients.raw: 2 white onions (1 halved for poaching, 1 thinly sliced for tinga)

ingredients.name: garlic cloves
ingredients.raw: 6 garlic cloves (3 for poaching, 3 minced for tinga)

ingredients.name: fine sea salt
ingredients.raw: 1 tsp fine sea salt, plus more to taste

ingredients.name: chipotle chillies in adobo sauce
ingredients.raw: 3 chipotle chillies in adobo sauce, plus 2 tbsp of the sauce

ingredients.name: adobo sauce
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp adobo sauce (from the chipotle tin)

ingredients.name: limes
ingredients.raw: 3 limes (2 juiced for slaw, 1 cut into wedges to serve)

ingredients.name: fresh coriander (cilantro)
ingredients.raw: 1 small bunch fresh coriander (cilantro), leaves and stems finely chopped

ingredients.name: white onion (for garnish)
ingredients.raw: 1/2 white onion, finely diced, to garnish

ingredients.name: fresh coriander leaves (for garnish)
ingredients.raw: Extra fresh coriander leaves, to garnish

ingredients.name: crumbled queso fresco or feta
ingredients.raw: 80 g crumbled queso fresco or feta, to serve

steps: Place the chicken thighs in a large saucepan with the halved onion, 3 whole garlic cloves, bay leaves, peppercorns, and 1 tsp salt. Cover with cold water by at least 5 cm. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer and cook for 25–30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and tender.

While the chicken poaches, make the lime slaw. Combine the shredded white and red cabbage in a large bowl. Add the juice of 2 limes, white wine vinegar, sugar, and chopped coriander. Season with salt, toss well, and refrigerate until ready to serve.

Transfer the cooked chicken thighs to a plate and reserve 250 ml of the poaching liquid. Once cool enough to handle, discard the skin and bones and shred the meat into generous strips using two forks.
Blend the chipotle chillies, adobo sauce, chopped tomatoes, and 3 minced garlic cloves together in a blender or food processor until you have a smooth, deep-red sauce.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large, heavy frying pan or cazuela over medium-high heat. Add the thinly sliced onion and cook, stirring, for 6–8 minutes until softened and beginning to char at the edges.
Pour the chipotle-tomato sauce into the pan — it will sizzle. Add the dried Mexican oregano and ground cumin. Cook, stirring constantly, for 4–5 minutes until the sauce darkens and thickens slightly.

Add the shredded chicken to the pan and stir to coat every strand in the sauce. Pour in 150 ml of the reserved poaching liquid, stir, and simmer over medium heat for 8–10 minutes until the tinga is juicy but not watery. Season generously with salt.
Heat a dry comal or cast-iron skillet over high heat. Warm the corn tortillas for 30–40 seconds per side until pliable with a few light char spots. Stack under a clean cloth to keep warm.

Build the tacos: lay two tortillas slightly overlapping on each plate. Spoon a generous heap of chicken tinga onto each, then top with lime slaw, sliced avocado, finely diced raw white onion, crumbled queso fresco, and a scatter of fresh coriander leaves.
Serve immediately with lime wedges alongside for squeezing.
_brief: Chicken tinga tacos with lime slaw

title: Black Bean & Sweet Potato Enchiladas
description: Hearty roasted sweet potato and smoky black bean enchiladas smothered in a rich, authentic guajillo-tomato sauce and melted cheese — a vibrant, soul-warming Mexican classic.

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes
ingredients.raw: 500 g sweet potatoes, peeled and diced into 1 cm cubes

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: black beans (canned, drained and rinsed)
ingredients.raw: 400 g canned black beans, drained and rinsed

ingredients.name: dried guajillo chillies
ingredients.raw: 4 dried guajillo chillies, stems and seeds removed

ingredients.name: dried ancho chilli
ingredients.raw: 1 dried ancho chilli, stem and seeds removed

steps: Preheat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan / Gas 7).

Toss the diced sweet potato with 2 tbsp olive oil, the cumin, smoked paprika, a generous pinch of salt and black pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking tray and roast for 20–25 minutes, turning once halfway, until tender and caramelised at the edges.

Meanwhile, make the enchilada sauce: toast the dried guajillo and ancho chillies in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 30–40 seconds per side until fragrant. Submerge them in a bowl of just-boiled water and soak for 15 minutes until soft, then drain.

Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a saucepan over a medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook, stirring, for 6–7 minutes until softened and lightly golden. Add 3 of the garlic cloves (finely chopped) and cook for a further 1 minute.

Transfer the softened onion and garlic to a blender along with the soaked chillies, canned tomatoes, vegetable stock, oregano and apple cider vinegar. Blitz until completely smooth. Season with salt to taste.
Pour the sauce back into the saucepan and simmer over a medium-low heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened slightly. Keep warm.
In a bowl, combine the roasted sweet potato, black beans and the remaining garlic clove (minced). Taste and adjust seasoning.
Reduce the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan / Gas 5). Spread a ladleful (about 100 ml) of the enchilada sauce over the base of a large, deep baking dish (approx. 30 × 22 cm).
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry frying pan for 20–30 seconds per side (or wrap in a damp tea towel and microwave for 60 seconds) to make them pliable.

Working one at a time, dip each tortilla briefly into the warm enchilada sauce to lightly coat it, then lay it flat and spoon 2–3 heaped tablespoons of the sweet potato and black bean filling down the centre. Roll tightly and place seam-side down in the baking dish. Repeat with all tortillas.
Pour the remaining enchilada sauce evenly over the rolled tortillas, then scatter the grated Oaxaca cheese over the top.
Bake for 18–20 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling and the edges of the tortillas are just beginning to crisp.
Remove from the oven and rest for 5 minutes. Garnish with fresh coriander and pickled jalapeños, and serve with soured cream and lime wedges on the side.
_brief: Black bean and sweet potato enchiladas

title: Birria de Res Tacos with Consommé
description: Deeply spiced, slow-braised beef tacos crisped in a rich chilli-red consommé, served with the fragrant dipping broth for the ultimate authentic birria experience.

ingredients.name: beef chuck
ingredients.raw: 500 g beef chuck, cut into large chunks

ingredients.name: dried guajillo chillies
ingredients.raw: 5 dried guajillo chillies, stems and seeds removed

ingredients.name: dried ancho chillies
ingredients.raw: 3 dried ancho chillies, stems and seeds removed

ingredients.name: dried chipotle chillies
ingredients.raw: 2 dried chipotle chillies, stems and seeds removed

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: Oaxaca or mozzarella cheese
ingredients.raw: 200 g Oaxaca or mozzarella cheese, shredded

steps: Toast the dried guajillo, ancho, and chipotle chillies in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30–60 seconds per side until fragrant. Transfer to a bowl, cover with boiling water, and soak for 20 minutes until softened.

In the same skillet over high heat, char the halved onion, unpeeled garlic cloves, and roma tomatoes cut-side down for 4–5 minutes until blackened in spots. Peel the garlic once cool enough to handle.

Drain the soaked chillies and add them to a blender along with the charred onion, garlic, tomatoes, apple cider vinegar, cumin, oregano, cinnamon, cloves, and 250 ml of the beef stock. Blend on high until completely smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing firmly, and discard solids.

Season the beef short ribs and chuck generously with salt and black pepper. Heat a splash of oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over high heat and sear the beef in batches for 3–4 minutes per side until deeply browned all over. Remove and set aside.

Pour the blended chilli sauce into the same pot and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring, until it darkens slightly and reduces. Add the remaining beef stock, bay leaves, and seared beef. Bring to a boil.
Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid, reduce the heat to its lowest setting, and braise for 3 to 3.5 hours until the beef is completely tender and falling off the bone.
Remove the beef from the pot. Discard the bay leaves and bones. Shred the beef using two forks, then stir it back into the consommé. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt.
Skim the red fat that has risen to the surface of the consommé and pour it into a small bowl — this achiote-red fat is key for frying the tacos.

Heat a large skillet or griddle over medium-high heat. Dip each corn tortilla into the consommé briefly to coat, then lay it in the skillet. Add a spoonful of shredded beef and a pinch of shredded cheese to one half of the tortilla. Fold over and press gently. Brush the outside with the reserved red fat and cook for 2 minutes per side until crispy and golden.

Ladle the hot consommé into small bowls for dipping. Serve the crispy tacos immediately alongside the bowls of consommé, garnished with diced white onion, fresh cilantro, and lime wedges for squeezing.
_brief: Slow-braised beef tacos with a rich dipping broth

title: Chipotle & Dark Chocolate Chilli con Carne
description: A rich, smoky, deeply flavoured chilli con carne slow-simmered with fiery chipotle chillies and finished with a whisper of dark chocolate for an authentic Mexican depth.

ingredients.name: beef chuck
ingredients.raw: 600g beef chuck, cut into 1.5 cm dice

ingredients.name: kidney beans (drained and rinsed)
ingredients.raw: 400g tin kidney beans, drained and rinsed

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: lime
ingredients.raw: 1 lime, cut into wedges, to serve

steps: Rehydrate the chipotle chillies: place them in a small bowl, cover with 150ml of boiling water and soak for 15 minutes until soft. Remove the stems and seeds, then blend or finely chop the flesh. Reserve the soaking liquid.
Pat the beef chuck dry with kitchen paper and season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large, heavy-based Dutch oven or casserole over high heat. Working in two batches, sear the beef for 3–4 minutes per batch until deeply browned on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp of oil. Add the diced onion and green pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, for 8 minutes until softened and lightly golden.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato purée, ground cumin, ground coriander, smoked paprika, dried oregano and cinnamon. Cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes to toast the spices.
Return the seared beef to the pot. Add the chopped tomatoes, beef stock, the prepared chipotle paste and the reserved chipotle soaking liquid. Stir well to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low. Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beef is very tender.
Stir in the drained kidney beans and the apple cider vinegar. Simmer uncovered for a further 15 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Remove from heat and stir in the finely chopped dark chocolate until fully melted and incorporated. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle into warmed bowls, garnish with fresh coriander and a dollop of soured cream. Serve with lime wedges and warm corn tortillas or steamed rice.
_brief: Chilli con carne with chipotle and dark chocolate

title: Chicken Katsu Curry
description: Crispy golden panko-crusted chicken cutlets served over fluffy steamed rice and smothered in a velvety, mildly spiced Japanese curry sauce.

ingredients.name: plain flour
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp plain flour (for the curry sauce)

ingredients.name: spring onions
ingredients.raw: 2 spring onions, finely sliced, to garnish

steps: Rinse the short-grain rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Place in a saucepan with 360ml cold water, bring to a boil, then reduce to the lowest heat, cover tightly, and cook for 12 minutes. Remove from the heat and leave to steam, covered, for 10 minutes.

While the rice cooks, make the curry sauce. Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the diced onion and carrot and cook gently for 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until very soft and beginning to caramelise.
Add the garlic and ginger to the pan and cook for a further 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the curry powder and garam masala and cook for 1 minute to toast the spices. Add the 2 tbsp of plain flour and stir to coat, cooking for another minute.

Gradually pour in the chicken stock, a ladleful at a time, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Add the soy sauce, tonkatsu sauce, and honey. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens to a smooth, glossy consistency. Season with salt and white pepper. Keep warm on a low heat.
Place each chicken breast between two sheets of cling film and pound with a rolling pin to an even thickness of about 1.5cm.
Set up a breading station with three shallow dishes: one with flour seasoned with salt and white pepper, one with the beaten eggs, and one with the panko breadcrumbs.

Coat each chicken breast first in the seasoned flour (shake off any excess), then dip in the beaten egg, and finally press firmly into the panko breadcrumbs, ensuring an even, thorough coating on all sides.

Pour the vegetable oil into a large frying pan to a depth of about 1cm and heat to 170°C (340°F). Carefully lay the chicken cutlets in the oil and shallow-fry for 4–5 minutes per side until deeply golden and cooked through. Transfer to a wire rack or paper towels to drain.

Slice each chicken katsu diagonally into 2cm strips. Portion the steamed rice into bowls, fan the sliced katsu on top, and ladle the warm curry sauce generously over one side. Garnish with sliced spring onions and serve with pickled ginger on the side.
_brief: Chicken katsu curry

title: Salmon Teriyaki Donburi Rice Bowl
description: Glossy, caramelised salmon fillets glazed in a classic homemade teriyaki sauce, nestled over fluffy Japanese short-grain rice and finished with fresh toppings for an authentic donburi experience.

ingredients.name: neutral oil (e.g. vegetable or sunflower)
ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp neutral oil (e.g. vegetable or sunflower)

ingredients.name: nori sheet, cut into thin strips
ingredients.raw: 1 nori sheet, cut into thin strips

ingredients.name: Japanese mayonnaise (e.g. Kewpie)
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp Japanese mayonnaise (e.g. Kewpie), to drizzle

steps: Rinse the short-grain rice in cold water 3–4 times until the water runs nearly clear. Place in a saucepan with 360ml water, cover with a tight-fitting lid and bring to the boil over medium-high heat. Reduce to the lowest heat and cook for 12 minutes. Remove from heat and leave to steam, lid on, for a further 10 minutes. Do not lift the lid during cooking.
While the rice cooks, make the teriyaki sauce. Combine the soy sauce, mirin, sake and caster sugar in a small bowl and stir until the sugar dissolves. Set aside.
Pat the salmon fillets dry with kitchen paper — this ensures a good sear. Season lightly with a pinch of salt.

Heat the neutral oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Place the salmon fillets skin-side down and press gently with a spatula for the first 30 seconds. Cook for 3–4 minutes until the skin is golden and crisp, then flip and cook the flesh side for 2 minutes.

Reduce the heat to medium-low and pour the teriyaki sauce into the pan. Spoon the sauce continuously over the salmon for 1–2 minutes, allowing it to reduce into a thick, glossy glaze that coats the fish. Remove the pan from the heat.
Fluff the steamed rice with a rice paddle or fork using gentle folding motions. Divide the rice evenly between two large, deep bowls.
Place one glazed salmon fillet on top of each bowl of rice, skin-side up to keep it crisp. Spoon any remaining teriyaki glaze from the pan over the top.
Garnish with sliced spring onions, toasted sesame seeds, nori strips and pickled ginger on the side. Finish with a drizzle of Japanese mayonnaise. Serve immediately.
_brief: Salmon teriyaki donburi rice bowl

title: Miso-Glazed Aubergine (Nasu Dengaku) with Steamed Rice
description: Silky, caramelised aubergine halves lacquered with a sweet-savoury white miso glaze, served over fluffy Japanese steamed rice for a beautifully authentic weeknight dinner.

ingredients.name: neutral oil (e.g. sunflower or vegetable)
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp neutral oil (e.g. sunflower or vegetable)

ingredients.name: toasted sesame seeds
ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds, to garnish

ingredients.name: spring onions
ingredients.raw: 2 spring onions, finely sliced, to garnish

steps: Rinse the short-grain rice in cold water 3–4 times until the water runs almost clear. Drain and place in a medium saucepan with 360 ml cold water. Cover tightly, bring to the boil over medium heat, then reduce to the lowest heat and cook for 12 minutes. Remove from the heat and let it steam, lid on, for a further 10 minutes. Do not lift the lid during cooking.
While the rice cooks, preheat your grill (broiler) to high.
Score the cut face of each aubergine half in a deep crosshatch pattern, cutting almost to the skin. Brush both the cut face and skin generously with neutral oil.
Place the aubergine halves cut-side down on a foil-lined baking tray. Grill for 8 minutes until the skin begins to blister and the flesh softens.

Meanwhile, make the dengaku glaze: whisk together the white miso paste, mirin, sake, caster sugar, soy sauce, and sesame oil in a small saucepan over low heat. Stir continuously for 2–3 minutes until the sugar dissolves and the glaze thickens slightly to a spreadable consistency. Remove from the heat.
Flip the aubergine halves cut-side up. Spoon and spread the miso glaze evenly and generously over each cut surface.
Return the tray to the grill and cook for a further 5–7 minutes, watching closely, until the glaze is deeply caramelised, bubbling, and slightly charred at the edges.
Fluff the steamed rice gently with a rice paddle or fork.
Serve the miso-glazed aubergine halves over bowls of steamed rice. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and sliced spring onions. Sprinkle with shichimi togarashi at the table if desired.
_brief: Miso-glazed aubergine with steamed rice

title: Kung Pao Chicken with Peanuts
description: A fiery, glossy Sichuan classic with tender wok-tossed chicken, toasted peanuts, and dried chillies in a bold sweet-savoury sauce.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.raw: 400g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 2cm cubes

ingredients.name: dried Sichuan chillies (er jing tiao or similar)
ingredients.raw: 10 dried Sichuan chillies, halved and seeds shaken out

ingredients.name: spring onions
ingredients.raw: 4 spring onions, white parts cut into 2cm pieces, green tops sliced for garnish

ingredients.name: neutral oil (e.g. groundnut or vegetable)
ingredients.raw: 3 tbsp neutral oil (e.g. groundnut or vegetable)

steps: Marinate the chicken: combine the chicken cubes with 1 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tbsp Shaoxing rice wine, and 1 tsp cornstarch in a bowl. Mix well and leave to marinate for at least 15 minutes.

Make the sauce: in a small bowl whisk together 2 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp dark soy sauce, 1 tbsp Chinkiang black rice vinegar, 1 tbsp Shaoxing rice wine, 2 tsp caster sugar, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp cornstarch, and 2 tbsp cold water until the sugar and starch dissolve. Set aside.
Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry wok over medium heat for 60 seconds until fragrant, then crush coarsely using a pestle and mortar. Set aside.

Heat the wok over the highest flame until smoking. Add 2 tbsp of the oil, then stir-fry the marinated chicken in a single layer for 2–3 minutes without stirring to develop colour, then toss and cook for a further 1–2 minutes until just cooked through. Remove to a plate.

Reduce the heat slightly and add the remaining 1 tbsp of oil to the wok. Add the dried chillies and crushed Sichuan peppercorns and stir-fry for 30–45 seconds until the chillies darken and become fragrant — do not burn them.
Add the garlic, ginger, and the white parts of the spring onions. Stir-fry vigorously for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Return the chicken to the wok, pour the sauce over everything, and toss constantly over high heat for 1–2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken in a glossy glaze.
Add the peanuts and toss for a further 30 seconds so they warm through but retain their crunch.
Plate immediately and garnish with the sliced green spring onion tops. Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
_brief: Kung pao chicken with peanuts

title: Char Siu Pork with Steamed Pak Choi
description: Succulent Cantonese barbecue pork glazed in a sticky, fragrant char siu sauce, served alongside tender steamed pak choi for an authentic Chinese feast.

ingredients.name: pork shoulder or pork neck
ingredients.raw: 600g pork shoulder or pork neck, cut into 3cm-thick strips

ingredients.name: fermented red bean curd (nam yue)
ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp fermented red bean curd (nam yue), mashed — optional but authentic

ingredients.name: neutral oil
ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp neutral oil (e.g. vegetable or groundnut)

ingredients.name: light soy sauce (for pak choi)
ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp light soy sauce (for the pak choi)

ingredients.name: oyster sauce (for pak choi)
ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp oyster sauce (for the pak choi)

steps: Make the char siu marinade: in a large bowl, combine the hoisin sauce, oyster sauce, Shaoxing rice wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, 1 tbsp of the honey, brown sugar, sesame oil, five-spice powder, white pepper, minced garlic, and mashed red bean curd (if using). Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the pork strips to the marinade and turn thoroughly to coat. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight for maximum flavour.
When ready to cook, remove the pork from the fridge 30 minutes before roasting to bring it to room temperature. Preheat your oven to 220°C (200°C fan / Gas 7).

Line a roasting tin with foil and place a wire rack on top. Lift the pork strips from the marinade (reserving the marinade) and lay them on the rack. Pour 120ml of water into the base of the tin to prevent drips burning.
Roast the pork for 20 minutes, then flip the strips and brush liberally with the reserved marinade. Roast for a further 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, pour the remaining reserved marinade into a small saucepan with the remaining 1 tbsp of honey. Simmer over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until thickened into a glossy glaze. Set aside.

Switch the oven to the grill/broiler setting at high heat. Brush the pork generously with the thickened glaze and grill for 3–5 minutes, watching closely, until the edges are lightly caramelised and charred. Flip, glaze the other side, and grill for 2–3 minutes more. Remove and rest for 5 minutes.
Prepare the pak choi: bring a large pan of water to the boil and blanch the halved pak choi for 90 seconds until just tender but still vibrant green. Drain and arrange on a serving plate.

Heat the neutral oil in a small pan over high heat. Add the sliced garlic and fry for 30–45 seconds until golden and fragrant. Immediately spoon the hot garlic oil over the pak choi, then drizzle with the light soy sauce and oyster sauce.
Slice the rested char siu pork on the diagonal into 1cm pieces, brush with any remaining glaze, and serve alongside the pak choi and steamed jasmine rice.
_brief: Char siu pork with pak choi

title: Authentic Mapo Tofu with Sichuan Pepper
description: Silken tofu bathed in a fiery, numbing Sichuan pepper and doubanjiang sauce with fragrant minced pork — bold, lip-tingling, and utterly irresistible.

ingredients.name: silken tofu
ingredients.raw: 400 g silken tofu, cut into 2 cm cubes

ingredients.name: douchi (fermented black beans)
ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp douchi (fermented black beans), roughly chopped

ingredients.name: neutral oil
ingredients.raw: 3 tbsp neutral oil (e.g. vegetable or sunflower)

ingredients.name: spring onions
ingredients.raw: 3 spring onions, thinly sliced, to garnish

ingredients.name: steamed white rice
ingredients.raw: Steamed white rice, to serve (2 portions)

steps: Toast the Sichuan peppercorns and dried red chillies in a dry wok over medium heat for 1–2 minutes until fragrant. Transfer to a mortar and pestle and grind to a coarse powder. Set aside.
Bring a medium saucepan of lightly salted water to a gentle simmer. Carefully slide in the tofu cubes and poach for 2 minutes to firm them up slightly. Drain with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Mix the cornstarch with the cold water in a small bowl until a smooth slurry forms. Set aside.
Heat the neutral oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add the minced pork and stir-fry, breaking it up, for 3–4 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Push the pork to the side, reduce heat to medium, and add the doubanjiang to the empty side of the wok. Stir-fry the paste in the oil for 1–2 minutes until it darkens and releases its red colour.
Add the garlic, ginger, and douchi to the wok and stir everything together. Fry for a further 1 minute until intensely fragrant.
Pour in the chicken stock and light soy sauce, stir to combine, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Carefully slide the poached tofu into the wok. Spoon the sauce over the tofu gently — avoid stirring aggressively to keep the cubes intact. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Give the cornstarch slurry a quick stir, then drizzle it into the wok in two additions, gently pushing the sauce around the tofu after each addition, until the sauce thickens to coat the tofu.
Drizzle with sesame oil and scatter over the ground Sichuan pepper and chilli powder. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Ladle into bowls over steamed white rice, garnish generously with sliced spring onions, and serve immediately.
_brief: Mapo tofu with Sichuan pepper

title: Smoky BBQ Pulled Pork with Apple Slaw
description: Meltingly tender, smoke-kissed pulled pork slathered in a rich homemade BBQ sauce, piled high on brioche buns alongside a crisp, tangy apple slaw.

ingredients.name: dark brown sugar (for BBQ sauce)
ingredients.raw: 3 tbsp dark brown sugar (for BBQ sauce)

steps: Preheat your oven to 150 °C (300 °F) fan / 165 °C conventional.
In a small bowl, combine the smoked paprika, 2 tbsp dark brown sugar, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, cayenne, mustard powder, salt and black pepper to make the dry rub.
Pat the pork shoulder completely dry with kitchen paper. Score the fat cap in a crosshatch pattern, then massage the dry rub all over every surface of the pork, working it into the scores.
Place the pork fat-side up in a deep roasting tin or Dutch oven. Pour 120 ml of water into the base of the tin, then cover tightly with a lid or a double layer of foil.

Roast in the oven for 5 hours, then remove the foil and roast for a further 30 minutes to caramelise the outside. The pork is ready when it shreds easily with two forks and an internal temperature of at least 93 °C (200 °F) is reached.

Meanwhile, make the BBQ sauce. In a small saucepan over medium heat, soften the minced garlic in a splash of oil for 1 minute. Add the ketchup, 60 ml apple cider vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, 3 tbsp dark brown sugar, yellow mustard and hot sauce. Stir well, bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 10–12 minutes until thickened. Season to taste.

Make the apple slaw. In a large bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, 2 tbsp apple cider vinegar, caster sugar, celery seeds and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Add the shredded green and red cabbage, julienned apple and grated carrot. Toss everything together until evenly coated. Refrigerate until needed.

Once the pork is cool enough to handle, remove and discard the bone and any large pieces of fat. Use two forks (or your hands) to shred the meat into long strands directly in the roasting tin, mixing in any resting juices.
Pour roughly two-thirds of the BBQ sauce over the pulled pork and toss well to coat. Keep the remaining sauce at the table for topping.
Lightly toast the brioche buns cut-side down in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes until golden.
Pile a generous heap of saucy pulled pork onto each bun base, top with a mound of apple slaw, finish with an extra drizzle of BBQ sauce and press the lid on. Serve immediately.
_brief: Smoky BBQ pulled pork with apple slaw

title: Buttermilk Fried Chicken with Charred Corn
description: Crispy, golden buttermilk-soaked fried chicken paired with smoky, charred corn on the cob — a true taste of authentic American Southern comfort cooking.

ingredients.name: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
ingredients.raw: 4 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.raw: 1 litre vegetable oil, for deep frying

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp fresh flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.raw: 1 lemon, cut into wedges, to serve

steps: In a large bowl, whisk together the buttermilk, hot sauce, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp smoked paprika, cayenne pepper, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp black pepper to make the marinade.
Add the chicken pieces to the marinade, turn to coat thoroughly, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight for best results.

When ready to cook, prepare the dredge: in a large shallow dish, combine the plain flour, cornstarch, baking powder, remaining garlic powder, onion powder, remaining smoked paprika, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Mix well.

Remove the chicken from the buttermilk marinade, allowing any excess to drip off. Press each piece firmly into the flour dredge, coating all sides thoroughly. Rest the coated chicken on a wire rack for 10 minutes to help the crust adhere.

Pour the vegetable oil into a large, deep heavy-bottomed pot (such as a Dutch oven) to a depth of about 8 cm and heat to 175°C (350°F) over medium-high heat, using a cooking thermometer to monitor temperature.

Working in batches to avoid crowding, carefully lower the chicken pieces into the hot oil. Fry for 13–15 minutes, turning once halfway through, until deeply golden and the internal temperature reads 75°C (165°F). Drain on a wire rack set over a baking tray.
While the last batch of chicken fries, heat a cast-iron griddle or heavy skillet over very high heat until smoking hot. Brush the corn cobs lightly with a little of the vegetable oil.
Char the corn cobs on the hot griddle for 8–10 minutes, turning every 2 minutes, until well charred and golden in spots all around.
Mix the softened butter with 1/2 tsp smoked paprika and a pinch of salt. Remove the corn from the heat and immediately rub all over with the smoked paprika butter.
Arrange the fried chicken and charred corn on a serving platter. Sprinkle with fresh parsley and serve with lemon wedges on the side.
_brief: Buttermilk fried chicken with charred corn

title: New England Clam Chowder
description: A rich, velvety New England classic loaded with tender clams, chunky potatoes, and smoky bacon in a luscious cream broth.

ingredients.name: Yukon Gold potatoes
ingredients.raw: 450 g Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1 cm cubes

ingredients.name: canned chopped clams
ingredients.raw: 2 x 280 g cans chopped clams, drained (juice reserved)

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.raw: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp fresh flat-leaf parsley, chopped, to garnish

steps: In a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat, cook the bacon lardons until crispy and the fat has rendered, about 6–8 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving the drippings in the pot.

Add the butter to the pot and melt over medium heat. Add the diced onion and celery and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for a further 1 minute.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir continuously for 2 minutes to cook out the raw flour taste.
Pour in the white wine and stir, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook for 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Add the clam juice (including the reserved juice from the canned clams), chicken stock, potatoes, bay leaves, and thyme sprigs. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered for 15–18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are completely tender when pierced with a fork.
Remove and discard the bay leaves and thyme sprigs. Using a potato masher or the back of a spoon, lightly crush some of the potatoes directly in the pot to thicken the chowder.
Stir in the drained clams and the heavy cream. Return to a gentle simmer (do not boil) and cook for 5 minutes until the clams are heated through and the chowder has thickened.
Season generously with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Ladle into warmed bowls, top with the reserved crispy bacon and a scattering of fresh parsley, and serve immediately with oyster crackers on the side.
_brief: New England clam chowder

title: Cajun Prawn & Sausage Jambalaya
description: A bold, smoky one-pot Cajun jambalaya packed with juicy prawns, spiced andouille sausage, and long-grain rice soaked in a rich, flavour-loaded tomato broth.

ingredients.name: raw king prawns, peeled and deveined
ingredients.raw: 300g raw king prawns, peeled and deveined

ingredients.name: andouille sausage (or smoked chorizo)
ingredients.raw: 250g andouille sausage (or smoked chorizo), sliced into rounds

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.raw: 1 handful fresh flat-leaf parsley, chopped, to serve

ingredients.name: salt and black pepper
ingredients.raw: Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Pat the prawns dry with kitchen paper, season lightly with a pinch of Cajun seasoning and set aside in the fridge until needed.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the sliced sausage and fry for 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned on both sides. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving the rendered fat in the pot.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the diced onion, green pepper and celery (the Cajun 'holy trinity') to the pot. Sauté for 6–7 minutes, stirring frequently, until softened and lightly golden.
Stir in the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomato paste and stir it into the vegetables, cooking for 2 minutes to caramelise slightly.
Sprinkle in the Cajun seasoning, smoked paprika, oregano, thyme and cayenne pepper. Stir well to coat the vegetables in the spices and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes and chicken stock. Add the bay leaves and stir to combine. Bring the mixture to a vigorous boil.
Stir in the uncooked rice and return the browned sausage to the pot. Reduce the heat to low, place a tight-fitting lid on the pot, and simmer for 20 minutes — do not lift the lid during this time.

After 20 minutes, check that the rice has absorbed the liquid and is tender. Nestle the seasoned prawns into the rice, replace the lid, and cook for a further 5 minutes until the prawns are pink and cooked through.
Remove the bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished generously with sliced spring onions and chopped fresh parsley.
